correctness.rationale: An exact step decomposition computes the sorting-chamber operator norm as the maximum boundary of a fixed-cardinality binary word divided by the input cut weight. Every chamber and witness can be realized by a strict-order pair. For sine edge weights, a central alternating block attains all change-count upper bounds; elementary sine sums establish parity-dependent sharpness. A fixed irreducible nonnegative central-cut matrix acts on the positive sine profile by the claimed eigenvalue. Its positive left Perron vector proves global lower bound and equality forces the unique sine ray. CHECK.py reproduces all binary words through n=11, matrix identities through n=250, and actual strict-chamber pairs; finite tests are corroborative, not an all-n proof.
